sections.heading: Motivation
paragraphs: Per the file, one of the fundamental (per the file) requirements of a Solana (per the file) client is access to (per the file) the status of a confirmed tx. Per the file, this is due to the fact that txs are not guaranteed to (per the file) be confirmed once submitted, (per the file) and may fail once executed. Per the file, virtually all Solana clients (per the file) therefore use a subscription-based (per the file) or polling mechanism to inquire whether a tx was successfully executed. Per the file, the only standard mechanism to retrieve tx statuses remotely is via the RPC protocol. Per the file, however, the RPC protocol (per the file) only serves replay information (per the file) of the RPC service itself. Per the file, it fails to provide information whether the node network at large has (per the file) derived the same information.

Per the file, this may allow an (per the file) RPC provider to send (per the file) incorrect information to a client, including marking a failed tx as successful. Per the file, solana node nodes replay all txs and thus have access to tx status information. Per the file, to improve security, clients should verify that tx status information received via RPC matches the node network at large. The file introduces a new “tx receipt” data structure, which (per the file) contains a subset of (per the file) the information available via RPC. Per the file, the derivation and serialization functions for tx receipts are defined to (per the file) be deterministic to prevent malleability. Per the file, to succinctly detect tx receipt mismatches, this proposal (per the file) further introduces a commitment (per the file) scheme based on a (per the file) binary hash tree that (per the file) is constructed once per slot.
